title: Keel: A Frontier Model Teaches a Vision-Language Model by Rewriting Its Weights
read_level: full main text (Secs 1-5) and appendices A, B, C.9, D.3, D.5, D.6 (arXiv HTML v1); other appendix tables and figures skimmed; inline math dropped by extraction
why_wsp: Several independent GPT-6 Astra agents, given a failure census and visual instruments but no gradients (autograd/optimisers disabled in the kernel), locate thinking-loop directions in Qwen3.5 VLM weights and write edits to attention output projections; the harness selects among editors on held-out questions.
facets: application domain: vision-language models (visual math, hallucination, GUI grounding)
domain: VLM thinking-loop repair on image benchmarks
editor: GPT-6 Astra with maximal reasoning effort, via API, run as multiple independent editors
target: Qwen3.5-0.8B and Qwen3.5-2B (natively multimodal; 24-layer LM, width 1,024 / 2,048)
interface: code/tensor tools (persistent CPU-only Python kernel with autograd disabled; generation passes, teacher-forced reads, blank-image reads, attention maps)
loop: closed-loop with feedback (40 forward passes per editor, up to 260 turns or 14 h) plus selection among independent editors on 1,000 held-out questions
self_editing: no; GPT-6 Astra edits Qwen3.5 VLMs
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: 0.8B Keel edit (editor 7): 22.67M changed weights; 2B union of editors 1+2: 2.46M (Table 9). "Only 15 attention output projections in zero-indexed language layers 8-22 were edited" (B.5). Second-round edit "changes six numbers" (D.5).

headline_results.where: Table 1 (Keel on 0.8B starts from the MIT prior edit)

headline_results.quote: On 2B directional ablation kept no edit.
the edit removes most loops on every benchmark, shortens the answers and makes the model significantly more accurate on average

headline_results.claim: Starting from the MIT prior edit
headline_results.quote: It is more accurate than the original weights on the 1,000 held-out questions (39.7% vs. 36.2%)
Every edit Keel selects from the original weights changes only attention output projections; none touches the vision encoder or the MLPs.

cost.quote: Editor turns 104 ... Forward passes 40 ... Editor input tokens (mostly cached) 3.9M ... Editor output tokens 168k

cost.where: Table 5 (turns, code runs, passes, conversations, hours, input, output)

cost.quote: Each alternates its own analysis code with forward passes until its 40 passes are spent, over 7.6 to 11.8 hours

baselines_and_controls: Thinking model as released; presence penalty; reflection suppression; budget forcing; automated directional ablation within same forward-pass budget; MIT prior edit (with/without budget forcing); ablations removing census, repair objective, visual instruments, and each edit step; editor-run norm-matched orthogonal-direction and amplification controls (reported by the editor, B.5).
runs_and_variance: One sample per question; paired bootstrap over questions (10,000 resamples); 3 editors (0.8B) and 4 editors (2B) per pool, every editing run listed in Table 9 with SE; "A single editing session is not reliable" (Sec 2.5).
robustness_of_edits: Transfer to benchmarks absent from the practice pool (GUI grounding, object probing); combination with budget forcing; editing on top of a prior edit and a second round. Not tested under fine-tuning or quantization.
verification: Statistical: held-out repair test (cut share lowered by >2 SE and accuracy gain positive), paired bootstrap; kernel enforces no-gradient constraint ('Autograd and optimisers are disabled').
memorization_vs_reasoning: Editors report causal tests in their own words (dose-response, amplification worsens loops, orthogonal controls); independent editors converge on middle-layer attention outputs (Fig 9). No direct test of recall vs derivation.
limitations_stated: Single editing sessions unreliable (some end with no edit); editor pools differ between models; selection rule chosen per model; costs are several API hours per run. (No dedicated limitations section found in main text.)
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al. 2026 Sparks of Weight-Space Programming blog [45] and released 0.8B edit
notes_for_survey: Extends the MIT loop-repair edit to VLMs with images given to the editor, a failure census, a repair objective that uses loop share rather than accuracy, and harness-side selection among several editors. On 0.8B the final Keel result stacks on the MIT prior edit; on 2B it starts from original weights.
